Definition: to strike with more or less violence (beat, fell, corrode); by implication (of attack) to knock together, i.e. surround or circulate
BiblicalUsage: Naqaph means to strike around or compass about, and it is used for the knops that ring the great sea in the temple. In 1 Kings 7:24 under the brim of the sea there are knops compassing it round about, ten in a cubit, cast in two rows, and in 2 Chronicles 4:3 the same oxen compass it round about in the same pattern.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the compassing knops are a picture of worship that goes all the way around; the sea is ringed on every side, and the work is finished on every side.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
